detail.runner_up_case: The strongest honest case for FALSE: the verdict rests entirely on secondary journalism echoing a single October 2025 announcement. No primary record has been pulled - no White House announcement, no DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney entry, no Federal Register item - so the team is certifying a claim no government document directly confirms. The details were contested in real time: FactCheck.org's November 2025 piece exists precisely because Trump's own account of the pardon was disputed, and the reported signing date wobbles (CBS says October 21; most outlets say only 'October'), a pattern consistent with outlets copying one another rather than independently verifying. Worse, four of the supporting articles (NYT, Straits Times, cryptorank, tradingview, all dated 2026-10-04 or later) postdate the 2026-10-01 as-of date and cannot support the verdict, thinning the base to sources that all descend from the same initial reports. If the original report mischaracterized the clemency action - a commutation rather than a pardon, a grant that was never completed, or coverage conflating CZ with another recipient - and was quietly corrected, this evidence pattern is exactly what an echo chamber looks like. That is the best honest case for FALSE; it remains a distant runner-up because the pre-as-of-date sources (CBS 60 Minutes 2025-11-17, FactCheck.org 2025-11-12, CNBC 2026-01-20/23, Brennan Center 2026-02-19, The Hill 2026-05-07) are independent, mainstream, mutually consistent on both the fact and the month, and none reports any retraction or revocation.
would_flip_it: A primary record - the DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney clemency list, a White House statement, or the Federal Register - that omits Changpeng Zhao or shows the October 2025 action was something short of a presidential pardon (e.g., a commutation or a grant that was never signed).
Any credible report or official statement dated before 2026-10-01 that the pardon was revoked, rescinded, withdrawn, or declared invalid.
A retraction or material correction from the originating October 2025 report showing the 'pardon' was misreported or concerned a different person (namesake confusion).
A court ruling issued before 2026-10-01 holding the pardon void or unenforceable.
